answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: the record's ticket_sha256 is the hash of the ticket PLAN file as it stood when the check ran, and a git revision with those bytes exists whenever the ticket was committed before the check (ee4e shows it can be absent, which is why absent means stale). Also load-bearing: plan fields are the right notion of 'the ticket changed'; the cursor lives in the state file, but some flows write workflow_and_state into the plan doc, so comparing only plan_fields keeps a crossing from making every record stale. Not assumed: that git is always available to the machine; without it the record stands only on an exact whole-file hash match.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: the file and the two functions to read (check at line 180, standing at 295), the exact predicate (three conditions plus the conservative fallback), the plan-field source (the ticket charter, never a hand list), the idempotent question path, and the proof's scratch git world (copy the existing proofs' door.set_diagnostic_roots pattern and make the scratch commons a git repo). The ticket carries all of these.
answers.children: none, because the change is one predicate and one reuse branch in one machine, with one proof
answers.collision_check: Looked at the machine's own D2 ('the outline is read on every run, never cached'; reuse keyed on the outline's hash does not cache the outline), the sieve ticket (the same predicate, spelled again in build_inspector, which 93fa3e3a6199 is moving) and the integrator's scratch script this replaces. The integrator's walk calling outlinecheck every time is the second caller this changes: after this it reuses a fresh record.
answers.falsifier_check: Clauses: (1) a fresh record is reused with zero reader calls and no new record, and a cursor-only change keeps it fresh | (2) a changed outline, a changed plan field, or an unfindable revision re-runs the check; --force re-runs a fresh one. Horizon: red on current main (check always reads), green after; proven over a scratch git commons with a counting fake reader.
answers.gates_bound: proof gate (a hollow build must fail it) + durability gate (committed) + feeds-back-to-origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8).
answers.missing_check: Not wrapped: how the machine finds the commons repo root and the ticket's relative path under it for the git calls (door.roots()['CairnCommons'] and the ticket file's path), and what happens in a scratch commons that is not a git repo (the proof's world is a real scratch git repo). Also unmeasured: the cost of walking a long ticket history; the integrator's script does it per call and it was acceptable.
